business_ops.supply_chain_integration: Backward integration: the Group has secured mining permits for one Barite mine and one Copper mine, both in Morocco, stated to secure supplies at low mining cost and de-risk the business from price shocks. The Barite mining permit (No. 3739267, Ighoud Commune, Youssoufia Province, Marrakech-Safi Region, Morocco) covers an area estimated on geological assessment reports to contain approximately 0.75 million MT of Barite ore at an average grade of 4.25; the mining licence is expected by end-June 2026 or mid-July 2026, after which commercial extraction and sale are proposed to commence. The planned copper mining operations, supported by an on-site flotation unit, are intended to enable copper cathode production via third-party smelters. Pending own mining, procurement is anchored by the Morocco subsidiary Atlas Resources International, which buys Barite and Fluorspar from Moroccan miners under long-term supply agreements: (i) agreement dated January 1, 2022 for purchase of Mixed Barite Fluorspar, valid till December 30, 2028, and (ii) agreement dated January 1, 2023 for purchase of Drilling Grade Barite 4.20 density API Grade, valid till December 30, 2027. Atlas has executed 100% of its sales to the Company and to Geo Min Commodities Pte. Ltd., Singapore, which procures all Atlas-sourced material and markets it in USA, Germany, Singapore, UAE, Oman and Suriname; Copper Cathode is procured from Chile through multiple trading partners across Singapore and the UAE. The Atlas-procurement / Geo Min-marketing structure is stated to be designed to take advantage of different tax rates in Morocco and Singapore and to keep ultimate-buyer details within the Singapore entity. In India, the Company began trading Barite in FY2025 and is eligible to participate in Andhra Pradesh Mineral Development Corporation (APMDC) tenders (prior transaction experience being a mandatory requirement), with operations located 128 km from Krishnapatnam Port; the RHP states such tenders are open to other participants and may or may not be awarded to the Company. Forward integration: for drilling-grade barite serving oil & gas, the Company plans to install its own grinding mills to deliver product from its mines directly to oil rigs; for industrial-grade barite it plans milling, beneficiation and leaching plants to achieve barite sulphate purities of 96-97%. overview.business_model: Two revenue streams. (1) Minerals: the Company sells Barite and Fluorspar in India, while the international mineral business runs through wholly-owned subsidiary Geo Min Commodities Pte. Ltd. (Singapore), which acts as the global marketing and selling arm, and its step-down subsidiary Atlas Resources International (Morocco), which acts as the procurement arm; customers are in the United States, Germany, Suriname and Oman, serving oil & gas and chemical industries. Geo Min's operation is stated to be highly dependent on Copper Cathode sourced from a few key suppliers with no long-term supply agreements. (2) Rice bran oil: the Company extracts crude rice bran oil and refines it, plus sells associated residues and by-products (De-Oiled Rice Bran, Fatty Acids, Gums, Spent Earth and Wax), selling mainly in bulk to players who sell edible oil in unbranded/loose form and to re-packers. Stated installed capacity is 60,000 MT per annum solvent extraction and 15,000 MT per annum oil refinery as on the date of the RHP. Per the RHP, subsidiaries contributed 87.85% of consolidated revenue from operations for the period ended December 31, 2025 (FY2025: 86.11%; FY2024: 81.85%; FY2023: 70.24%).

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Backward integration: the Group has secured mining permits for one Barite mine and one Copper mine, both in Morocco, stated to secure supplies at low mining cost and de-risk the business from price shocks. The Barite mining permit (No. 3739267, Ighoud Commune, Youssoufia Province, Marrakech-Safi Region, Morocco) covers an area estimated on geological assessment reports to contain approximately 0.75 million MT of Barite ore at an average grade of 4.25; the mining licence is expected by end-June 2026 or mid-July 2026, after which commercial extraction and sale are proposed to commence. The planned copper mining operations, supported by an on-site flotation unit, are intended to enable copper cathode production via third-party smelters. Pending own mining, procurement is anchored by the Morocco subsidiary Atlas Resources International, which buys Barite and Fluorspar from Moroccan miners under long-term supply agreements: (i) agreement dated January 1, 2022 for purchase of Mixed Barite Fluorspar, valid till December 30, 2028, and (ii) agreement dated January 1, 2023 for purchase of Drilling Grade Barite 4.20 density API Grade, valid till December 30, 2027. Atlas has executed 100% of its sales to the Company and to Geo Min Commodities Pte. Ltd., Singapore, which procures all Atlas-sourced material and markets it in USA, Germany, Singapore, UAE, Oman and Suriname; Copper Cathode is procured from Chile through multiple trading partners across Singapore and the UAE. The Atlas-procurement / Geo Min-marketing structure is stated to be designed to take advantage of different tax rates in Morocco and Singapore and to keep ultimate-buyer details within the Singapore entity. In India, the Company began trading Barite in FY2025 and is eligible to participate in Andhra Pradesh Mineral Development Corporation (APMDC) tenders (prior transaction experience being a mandatory requirement), with operations located 128 km from Krishnapatnam Port; the RHP states such tenders are open to other participants and may or may not be awarded to the Company. Forward integration: for drilling-grade barite serving oil & gas, the Company plans to install its own grinding mills to deliver product from its mines directly to oil rigs; for industrial-grade barite it plans milling, beneficiation and leaching plants to achieve barite sulphate purities of 96-97%. In rice bran oil, the Company plans to sell a portion of refined oil under its own brand, creating a direct-to-consumer brand. Logistics: Port of Casablanca and Port of Agadir in Morocco for bulk and container shipments; planned investment in warehousing and port-based logistics support via the Singapore and Morocco subsidiaries; mineral testing/quality certification outsourced to Mitra S. K. Morocco SARL.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- The RHP's first risk factor states that 87.85%, 77.27%, 81.30% and 70.24% of consolidated revenue for the period ended December 31, 2025 and Fiscals 2025, 2024 and 2023 respectively came from subsidiaries; any loss of sales due to reduced demand for the subsidiaries' products would have a material adverse effect on business, financial condition, results of operations and cash flows. (Note: the FY2025 and FY2024 percentages in this risk-factor heading, 77.27% and 81.30%, do not reconcile with the 86.11% and 81.85% shown in the table immediately below it in the same risk factor.)
- The Company states it relies heavily on revenue generated from the sale of Barite, Fluorspar, Copper Cathode and other minerals, so any reduction in demand for these products directly hits results.
- Explicitly flagged twice in risk factor 1 - a downturn in the rice bran oil industry may adversely impact business, results of operations and financial condition.
- The RHP states success depends on the ability to diversify and grow operations and retain/expand customers for Barite, Fluorspar, Copper Cathode and other minerals; failure would cause revenue from operations and cash flow to decline, and there is no assurance such a decline will not occur.
- 86.11% of consolidated revenue in fiscal 2025 and 87.85% in the nine months ended December 31, 2025 came from outside India (UAE, Singapore, Oman, Germany, Suriname, USA), with the country mix shifting sharply between periods - UAE went from 35.75% of revenue in FY2025 to nil in the nine-month period.
- Only a mining permit (No. 3739267) has been allocated; the Company expects the mining licence by end June 2026 or mid-July 2026, and commercial extraction and sale of barite is only proposed to commence thereafter - so the backward-integration benefit is contingent on a pending regulatory approval.
- Copper cathodes are sourced from smelters in Chile with procurement diversified through multiple trading partners across Singapore and the UAE - the Company does not own the smelting source, and copper was 54.72% of fiscal 2025 consolidated revenue.
- Net Debt/EBITDA was 5.67 in FY2023 and 5.09 in FY2024, improving to 1.68 in FY2025 and 1.63 for the nine months ended December 31, 2025; Rs. 1,000 lakhs of Net Proceeds is earmarked for prepayment/repayment of certain loans.
